Two bugs in the REPL, both about where the cursor ends up.  (The word movement
in Ctrl+Left/Right arrived in 3.4.0, on the commit before these fixes.)

### A multi-line expression left a blank line under itself

```
>>> (go (do ((i 1 (+ i 1))) ((> i 10))
...   (chan-send! ch (* i i))))

>>> 
```

Submitting an expression drew it again without the cursor highlight and then
placed the cursor, moving it *down* by the number of newlines in the expression —
on the reasoning that writing the rows had left the cursor above the last one. It
had not: writing a row ends with the cursor on it, so the extra moves went past
the end, one blank line per newline in the form. A single-line expression has no
newline, moved nothing, and looked right, which is why only multi-line input
showed it.

### A wide character moved the cursor one column instead of two

```
>>> (display "中文")
```

The column the cursor was placed in was counted in characters rather than in
display columns, so every wide character before the cursor left it one cell
short — two for the line above, and the gap grew as more were typed. Typing,
backspace, Ctrl-A/E and Ctrl-Left/Right are all correct now.
